drown one's sorrows: After losing his job, he went to a bar every night to drown his sorrows instead of looking for new work.
失業後，他每晚都去酒吧借酒澆愁，而不是去找新工作。
drown out the noise: She turned up the music to drown out the noise of the traffic outside her window.
她把音樂開大聲，好蓋過窗外車流的噪音。
be drowned in work: With three reports due tomorrow, I am drowned in work and don't even have time for lunch.
明天要交三份報告，我被工作淹沒，連吃午餐的時間都沒有。
drowning in debt: After borrowing money to open a restaurant that failed, the young couple were drowning in debt.
借錢開的餐廳倒閉後，那對年輕夫妻債台高築。
dump waste: The factory was fined for illegally dumping waste into the river near the village.
那家工廠因為非法將廢棄物傾倒進村莊附近的河裡而被罰款。
dump a boyfriend: She finally decided to dump a boyfriend who never kept his promises and always lied to her.
她終於決定甩掉那個從不守信、總是對她說謊的男友。
dump stocks: When the bad news came out, investors rushed to dump stocks, and the market fell sharply.
壞消息一傳出，投資人便急著拋售股票，股市大幅下跌。
dump the blame on: Don't dump the blame on your little brother; I saw you break the vase yourself.
別把責任推給你弟弟，我親眼看到是你自己打破花瓶的。
dump products abroad: The company was accused of trying to dump products abroad at prices lower than the cost of making them.
這家公司被指控試圖以低於生產成本的價格向國外傾銷產品。
dust off an old plan: When the new manager arrived, she decided to dust off an old plan that had been forgotten for years.
新經理上任後，決定重拾一個被遺忘多年的舊計畫。
dust the furniture: Every Saturday morning, I help my mom dust the furniture and sweep the floors before guests come.
每個星期六早上，我都會在客人來之前幫媽媽撢家具和掃地。
bite the dust: Many small bookstores will bite the dust if people keep buying all their books online.
如果大家繼續在網路上買所有的書，許多小書店將會一敗塗地。
dwell on the past: There's no point in dwelling on the past; you should focus on what you can do now.
沉湎過去沒有意義，你應該專注在現在能做的事。
dwell on a mistake: Everyone makes errors, so don't dwell on a mistake for days; just learn from it and move on.
每個人都會犯錯，所以別好幾天都對一個錯誤耿耿於懷，從中學習然後往前走就好。
dwell in a cave: Thousands of years ago, early humans used to dwell in a cave to stay safe from wild animals.
數千年前，早期人類住在洞穴裡，以躲避野生動物的威脅。
dye one's hair: She decided to dye her hair bright pink for the school festival, and everyone noticed right away.
她決定為了校慶把頭髮染成亮粉紅色，大家馬上就注意到了。
dyed-in-the-wool: My grandfather is a dyed-in-the-wool baseball fan who has never missed a game on TV.
我爺爺是個徹頭徹尾的棒球迷，電視上的比賽他一場都沒錯過。
dye fabric: In this village, people still use plants and flowers to dye fabric in beautiful natural colors.
在這個村莊，人們仍用植物和花朵把布料染成美麗的天然色彩。
earn respect: By always keeping her promises, the new class leader quickly began to earn respect from her classmates.
新班長總是信守承諾，很快就贏得了同學的尊敬。
earn a reputation: Thanks to its fresh ingredients, the small noodle shop has earned a reputation as the best in town.
多虧新鮮的食材，這家小麵店博得了鎮上最好吃的名聲。
earn a living: After graduating, he found it hard to earn a living as an artist, so he also taught painting classes.
畢業後，他發現當藝術家很難謀生，所以也開了繪畫課。
earn a degree: She worked part-time in a café while studying to earn a degree in computer science.
她一邊在咖啡店打工，一邊讀書取得資訊工程學位。
earn interest: If you put your savings in the bank instead of under your bed, your money will earn interest over time.
如果你把存款放在銀行而不是床底下，你的錢會隨時間生利息。
earn one's keep: My parents say that if I live at home after graduation, I must earn my keep by doing housework.
我爸媽說，如果我畢業後住在家裡，就必須做家事自食其力。
echo one's views: In the meeting, several parents echoed his views, agreeing that students need more sleep and less homework.
會議中，幾位家長呼應他的看法，同意學生需要更多睡眠和更少的作業。
echo through the hall: When the famous singer walked on stage, loud cheers began to echo through the hall.
當那位知名歌手走上舞台時，響亮的歡呼聲開始迴盪大廳。
echo the sentiment: Many students echo the sentiment that the school library should stay open later during exam weeks.
許多學生呼應這個心聲，認為學校圖書館在考試週應該開晚一點。
echoes of the past: Walking through the old streets of Tainan, you can still hear echoes of the past in every temple.
走在台南的老街上，你仍能在每座廟宇中聽見過去的回音。
